decisions.reason: As a clearly marketed gas-tariff comparison close to the firm's core data and calculation capabilities, it is likely to stay unless results fall distinctly below aspiration levels.
This electricity tariff calculator fits the firm's central customer problems and platform trajectory, so management would usually retain it while it continues to support the core solution set.

Although its lighter web presence and multiple models raise rationalisation risk, it still builds on core capabilities and would more likely be kept while management evaluates which variants merit continued support.
The area-definition tool complements surrounding tariff and market-process offerings, making it useful to preserve as part of the broader platform even if direct demand is still developing.

Because it is only lightly presented, overlaps with nearby tariff-comparison offerings and is the most obvious candidate for problemistic search and resource reallocation after earlier portfolio pruning, management would now be inclined to withdraw it.
